neighbours.label: macroeconomics and political economy (national income, full employment, aggregate output, capitalism vs. socialism, and its authors), as opposed to the same frames about nature and places
fire: The chart tracks output, as measured by gross national income.
Keynes argued that it is possible to keep full employment.
Higher spending leads in the end to a rise in aggregate demand.
The debate is not about free markets vs. planning or capitalism vs. socialism.
Government deficits can raise aggregate demand in a slump.
Marx and Keynes both wrote about the crisis of capital.
A fall in investment lowers national output and wages.
See Thomas Piketty on inequality and the return on capital.
quiet: The chart tracks rainfall, as measured by gauges on the hills.
Darwin argued that it is possible to keep finches in cages.
Higher ground leads in the end to a view of the lake.
The debate is not about dogs vs. cats or tea vs. coffee.
Heavy clouds can bring rain in a valley.
Dickens and Austen both wrote about the life of families.
A fall in temperature lowers river levels and fog.
See Thomas Hardy on heaths and the villages of Dorset.

notes: Some peaks are on '.' after economics sentences. Near misses are easy.
